The debate over whether we have free Will is an ongoing one in philosophy, and there is not yet universal agreement on definitive answers. Several arguments can be cited as possible ways to explain it:

1. Dual-ascent: Some philosophers argue that at our deepest level, we possess a "dual-nature" which includes both body-matter (substantial) parts but also non-physical elements like desires or aspirations.

2. Internal Contradiction Resolution: It's often argued that if all behavior was entirely determined by physical law without any randomness, then there wouldn't actually exist any real contradictions - such situations would imply logic errors since contradictory actions could never happen. Thus, they postulate some kind of inherent freedom within us even while acknowledging science shows cause-and-effect relationships do prevail much of life.
